questions.def: 'Haven't' is the correct contraction of 'have not'.
questions.question: I ___ seen that movie before.

questions.def: 'Doesn't' is the correct negative form with 'she'.
questions.question: She ___ like coffee very much.

questions.def: 'Was' is incorrect; it should be 'were' with 'they'.
questions.question: They was not at home yesterday.

questions.def: 'Didn't eat' is the correct past simple negative form.
questions.question: I ___ breakfast this morning.

questions.def: 'Aren't' is the correct contraction of 'are not'.
questions.question: We ___ going to the party tonight.

questions.def: 'Didn't' is the past simple negative form of 'do not'.
questions.question: He said he ___ understand the question.

questions.def: 'Don't' is wrong; it should be 'doesn't' with 'she'.
questions.question: She don't like to eat meat.

questions.def: 'Don't want' is the correct present simple negative form.
questions.question: They ___ to come with us.

questions.def: 'Don't' is the correct negative form with 'I'.
questions.question: I ___ know the answer to that question.

questions.def: 'Isn't' is correct because 'milk' is uncountable.
questions.question: There ___ any milk in the fridge.

questions.def: 'Not' is missing the auxiliary verb 'is': He is not going.
questions.question: He not going to work today.

questions.def: 'Didn't make' is the correct past simple negative form.
questions.question: She ___ a cake yesterday.

questions.def: 'Haven't' is the correct present perfect negative form.
questions.question: They ___ finished their homework yet.

questions.def: 'Haven't' is correct present perfect negative auxiliary verb.
questions.question: We ___ seen him since last week.

questions.def: 'Not' is missing the auxiliary verb 'do': I do not like.
questions.question: I not like this music.

questions.def: 'Didn't go' is the correct past simple negative form.
questions.question: She ___ to the party last night.

questions.def: 'Doesn't' is the correct negative form with 'he'.
questions.question: He ___ speak Spanish very well.

questions.def: 'Couldn't' is correct past form of 'can not'.
questions.question: They said they ___ come to the meeting.

questions.def: 'Doesn't live' is the correct present simple negative form.
questions.question: He ___ in London now.

questions.def: 'Hadn't' is past perfect, suitable here.
questions.question: I ___ seen him at the party.

questions.def: 'Aren't' is correct for plural nouns.
questions.question: There ___ enough chairs for everyone.

questions.def: 'Not' requires auxiliary verb 'are'.
questions.question: We not going to the beach today.

questions.def: 'Doesn't work' is correct for 'she' in present simple.
questions.question: She ___ on Saturdays.

questions.def: 'Isn't' is the correct negative form with 'he'.
questions.question: He ___ going to be late.

questions.def: 'Haven't' is correct present perfect negative auxiliary verb.
questions.question: I ___ heard about that before.

questions.def: 'Isn't' should be 'aren't' with 'they'.
questions.question: They isn't coming to the party.

questions.def: 'Didn't see' is the correct past simple negative form.
questions.question: I ___ her yesterday.

questions.def: 'Don't need' is correct with 'you'.
questions.question: You ___ to worry about it.

questions.def: 'Doesn't' is the correct negative form with 'she'.
questions.question: She ___ have time to help you.

questions.def: Use 'haven't' with 'I' to make the negative present perfect.
questions.question: I ___ seen that movie before.
